newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 19.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
CONGRESS PARLIAMENTARY PARTY LEADER RAO ASKED TO STEP DOWN

Congress president Sitaram Kesri asked Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP) chief and former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao to step down from the CPP post. Earlier, the Congress Working Committee (CWC) had authorised the party president to hold talks with Rao in the light of the demand of the CPP executives for his resignation. A Rao confidant, however, said the CPP leader was not likely to oblige the party president. The CWC, in its another resolution, criticised the government for deteriorating economic situation in the country and asked it to take appropriate effective measures to reverse the trend.
The Economic Times
NEW PRIVATE BANKS ASKED TO MARK FULL PORTFOLIO TO MARKET

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has directed nine new private sector banks to mark 100 percent of their investment portfolio to market from the current year. This is against only 50 percent for all other banks. Bankers feel the central bank wants the new banks to adopt more stringent standards than others. To put Indian banks in line with international banks, which mark their entire portfolio to the market, the RBI has been raising the proportion of their portfolio that they must mark to market.
NEW PLAN TO DELICENSE SUGAR SECTOR

The Industry Ministry has proposed a new free licensing regime for the sugar industry. The uncertainty over an earlier delicensing proposal has prompted the ministry to make a new one. The ministry has also worked out a criteria for giving approvals to new sugar projects, proposals which envisage co-generation and the use of bagasse, and projects of international capacities. It has also suggested that the Food Ministry's role in granting fresh approvals be cut by way of winding up the screening panel for sugar projects, which it heads.
LONDON TRIBUNAL DROPS ENRON ARBITRATION

U.S. power compay Enron Corp said a London tribunal agreed to terminate arbitration proceedings started by its Indian unit, Dabhol Power company (DPC), against Maharashtra government. Both parties agreed that the guarantee by the state government would remain valid. DPC had initiated arbitration proceedings against the Maharashtra government after it cancelled the 2,450 megawatt power project in August 1995. It was later renegotiated.
Financial Express
B.A.T SEEKS REMOVAL OF ITC DIRECTORS

B.A.T Industries made a fresh offensive against ITC Ltd's executive board. The British multinational sought suspension of its Indian partner's remaining three wholetime directors, including chairman Y.C. Deveshwar. Sources said BAT cited several developments which had taken place after the ITC board meeting on November 15 for arriving at a conclusion that the remaining three executive directors also needed to be suspended.
BOMBAY BOURSE INDEX CROSSES 3,000 MARK

Pivotals moved widely on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on alternative bouts of buying and selling. The BSE sensitive index started slightly up at 2,986.02 and rose further to the session's high of 3,051.72, before closing at 3,OO1.24, still with a net gain of 17.22 points compared to the previous level of 2,984.02. The BSE-1OO index also edged up by 9.24 points to 1,322.15 from 1,312.91. The 50-share National Stock Exchange index fluctuated between 850.69 and 871.84 points, before closing down at 860.40 points as against its previous close of 850.74 points, showing a gain of 9.66 points.
HHS COMMUNICATIONS GETS ANOTHER EXTENSION

The Department of Telecommunications (DoT) has granted another three-month extension to the Hinduja-led HHS Communications. This is despite the fact that the consortium has not even been able to finalise its consortium partners until now. DoT sources said the latest extension until the end of February was given following the extension of bank guarantee by HHS Communications, the cellular licence holder for Tamil Nadu.
GOVERNMENT INSISTS ON ROYALTY REVIEW WITH SUZUKI

A protracted tussle between the federal government and Suzuki Motor of Japan, the two partners of Maruti Udyog Ltd, is in the offing again. The government is insisting on a review of the royalty agreement in April next year for Maruti 800 and Gypsy models. It has agreed to pay royalty to Suzuki up to April 1997 but has stipulated that the continuance of royalty payments and the rate of royalty for the remaining period of collaboration for the various models would be specifically reviewed on whether the desired transfer of technology has been effected. Sources said the government's decision to place a rider upon the technology pact renewal would prove to be a stumbling block for smooth relations between the two partners.
Business Standard
STOCK WATCH PARAMETERS LAID DOWN

The Securities and Exchange Board of India has laid down the basic framework for the StockWatch system to be introduced for the first time on the Indian bourses. The system is an advanced surveillance mechanism adopted by major stock exchanges throughout the world. Through its components -- alert segment, data analysis segment and report generation -- StockWatch system would enable identification of cases for further investigation.
INSURANCE MAJORS NOT TO LOSE MONOPOLY UNDER NEW BILL

The public sector Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) and General Insurance Corporation (GIC) would not lose their monopolies under a bill to be tabled in parliament to give statutory powers to the Insurance Regulatory Authority. Official sources said the bill would most probably be tabled on the last day of the current session of parliament, which was set to adjourn on Friday. The bill would, however, free both the companies of the powers that the Vigilance Commission had over them, sources added.
FIIS RAMPING SHARES FACE REGULATOR'S ACTION

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) plans to get tough on the foreign institutional investors (FIIs), who have been ramping the stock market. SEBI sources said there had been complaints pointing out instances where FIIs and their broking arms had ramped up prices and then offloaded their holdings in the market to reap huge profits. The bourse regulator would try to book the FII manipulators under its recently-framed regulations on unfair trade practices, sources added.
The Observer
GOLD POLICY BY FEBRUARY-END LIKELY

The Finance Ministry is likely to announce an integrated national gold policy (INGP) at the latest by February 28, 1997. The INGP would be based on an 11-point recommendation made by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI). RBI sources said the authorities felt that the time was now ripe for announcing the INGP in the wake of factors like erratic pricing of gold in the domestic market, recent spurt in gold smuggling, the need to sanitise Indian gold trade, and the need to discourage people from excessive craze for gold.
MINISTRY DROPS PLAN TO ALLOW NON-VOTING SHARES

The Finance Ministry dropped the proposal to allow non-voting shares in the wake of stiff opposition from different quarters. The Reserve Bank of India, Securities and Exchange Board of India and the Bombay Stock Exchange advised the ministry that the concept of non-voting shares was premature for the Indian market and could, therefore, have a deleterious effect on corporate democracy. The proposal sought to bring about an amendment to the Companies Act, making non-voting shares the third category of equities, other than the ordinary equity and the preferential.
